- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen next 3–5 periods by 3–7%.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model overestimates near-term upside — cap forecast growth at 2–4% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean reversion bias — adjust forecast toward recent 14-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows early downward correction after forecast peak, model is lagging — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates by 1–3% when sentiment is volatile — apply downward bias of 1.5–2.5% to final 5–7 periods.
